target.title: fix(infra): cache readMountEntries to avoid macOS/BSD performance penalty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where macOS/BSD database connections hit a heavy performance penalty (blocking the Node.js event loop for 10ms to 50ms) on every database open/probe. Since `/proc/self/mountinfo` is unavailable on non-Linux platforms, OpenClaw falls back to spawning `mount` synchronously via `childProcess.execFileSync("mount", [])` on every DB initialisation and query probe.

## Why This Change Was Made

We introduced global caching for parsed mount entries (`cachedMountEntries`) with a short 10-second TTL (`MOUNT_CACHE_TTL_MS = 10_000`). This avoids repeated synchronous child process spawns for subsequent database operations while still allowing eventual consistency if mount points change.

## User Impact

Resolves event loop blocking during SQLite WAL maintenance initialization and session queries on macOS/BSD, drastically improving database open latency.

## Evidence

### Unit Test Execution
We added unit tests verifying that `readMountEntries` caches the mount command execution and respects TTL:
```
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/sqlite-wal.test.ts (35 tests) 152ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
   Start at  23:37:40
   Duration  786ms (transform 420ms, setup 392ms, import 97ms, tests 152ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 7.59s
```

### Real Behavior Proof
The unit test `caches mount command results globally and respects TTL` mocks the `mount` execution and confirms that:
1. The first call to `configureSqliteWalMaintenance` triggers the `execFileSync` command.
2. Subsequent database connections and WAL maintenance configurations within the 10-second TTL do not spawn additional child processes (cached).
3. Advancing the timer past 10 seconds invalidates the cache and triggers a fresh `execFileSync` command.
